transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-12-30
Start: 10:00 AM PST
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Laura Martinez (SummitBank - Head of Security), Daniel Brooks (SummitBank - Platform Eng), Maya Patel (SummitBank - DevOps), Omar Ruiz (SummitBank - Legal)

Auto-generated Summary (brief):
- Quick status: POC running, model endpoints stable.
- Main security topics: SSO/SAML, audit logs, log forwarding to SIEM, retention policies, SOC2 evidence, KMS integration for keys.
- Next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 artifacts and run SSO-enabled benchmark; SummitBank to share SIEM endpoints and retention reqs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll do a quick 45 minute sync. quick roll call — Alex, Priya and Jordan from Redwood, and from SummitBank Laura, Daniel, Maya and Omar. sound good?
[00:10] Laura Martinez: Yep thanks, Laura here. we'll focus on the security items today, want to make sure nothing's blocking the pilot.
[00:16] Priya Nair: Great, I'll kick off with what we changed this week — we enabled basic audit logging in the POC cluster and pushed an updated image with KMS envelope support, so server side keys now can be backed by Redwood KMS integration, um, though we haven't wired customer KMS yet in the sandbox.
[00:32] Daniel Brooks: Quick question, Priya — when you say KMS integration, is that customer-managed keys? we need to know if we can use our AWS KMS alias or if it's Redwood-managed.
[00:39] Priya Nair: At the moment in hosted POC it's Redwood-managed for the sandbox; for Private and Dedicated we support customer KMS via external key provider, you can bring your own. we'll document exact flow.
[00:50] Laura Martinez: Is that HSM backed? we need to confirm for our security review.
[00:54] Alex Chen: Good call — our SOC2 artifacts note support for HSM-backed providers where customers opt in; we'll attach details.
[01:02] Omar Ruiz: From legal, we also need to see key rotation policy and evidence of key management controls.
[01:07] Jordan Lee: Noted, we'll include key rotation documentation and timeline in the pack.
[01:12] Maya Patel: On audit logs — we tried pulling logs last week, but the format was a bit noisy; timestamps look off sometimes, and user ids were anonymized as expected but we need correlation IDs. can the logs include request ids that we can map back to our app traces?
[01:26] Priya Nair: Yes — we do emit a request_id per call; I need to check whether the POC export template we used included it. sounds like we missed that flag. we'll re-export with request_id and correlation_id fields.
[01:35] Daniel Brooks: Also, retention — what's the default? We need to decide retention length and whether logs can be forwarded to our SIEM (Sumo/Elastic).
[01:42] Priya Nair: Default retention in the POC is 90 days; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention via policy. We support forwarding to external SIEMs via syslog or secure HTTP.
[01:52] Laura Martinez: Our compliance team requires 7 years for certain records, but for request-level transcripts we typically keep 1 year; also need proof they can't be read by unauthorized staff.
[02:03] Alex Chen: For hosted we maintain access controls and RBAC; we can provide audit of internal accesses. For Private deployments, data never leaves customer network. We'll surface the exact access controls in the document pack.
[02:14] Maya Patel: Regarding SSO, we started to try SAML with the test idp and it failed — assertion consumer URL mismatch. Any tips?
[02:21] Priya Nair: We had one change — ACS needs to be exactly the callback URL we issue. I will re-share the metadata and also a small troubleshooting checklist.
[02:29] Daniel Brooks: Is SSO enforced for the API too or just console? we want to lock down both.
[02:34] Priya Nair: Good question — SSO currently controls access to the console and management plane. API keys can be rotated and scoped; we also support short-lived tokens tied to SSO sessions for programmatic access in the Dedicated/Private variants.
[02:46] Laura Martinez: For the POC we need programmatic audit too — every API call mapped to a user or service account. can you show sample logs with that mapping?
[02:55] Priya Nair: We'll capture a sample, yes. we'll include an example row with user, request_id, model, prompt_hash, and timestamp.
[03:03] Alex Chen: Quick update on SOC2 — we have Type II report; I can share redacted version of the report and the pen test summary. note that some vendor details are redacted for public docs, but we'll provide the full to your security team under NDA.
[03:16] Omar Ruiz: NDA's already signed but we'll need the full under our vendor portal. I'll check with procurement.
[03:22] Jordan Lee: Great.
[03:24] [03:24] (crosstalk) Daniel Brooks: A tiny thing on network — if we go Private we need to validate egress rules, the model pulls can open outbound connections?
[03:33] Priya Nair: For Private deployments we can lock egress and allow only certain endpoints; models are pulled during deployments and can be cached behind your network. we'll provide the list of outbound domains and IP ranges.
[03:44] Maya Patel: Can you provide the manifest of ports/protocols? our firewall team will ask.
[03:48] Alex Chen: Yup, we'll include a network manifest doc.
[03:51] Laura Martinez: One more — audit log integrity: do you support append-only logs or signed logs to prove non-repudiation?
[03:59] Priya Nair: We don't currently sign logs with customer keys, but we maintain WORM-like retention and have tamper-evident controls internally — I can capture the technical detail and potential roadmap to support signed logs for Private customers.
[04:12] Laura Martinez: That would be helpful, if it's a roadmap we need to understand timing.
[04:17] Priya Nair: I'll add it as an item with an estimated timeline.
[04:20] Alex Chen: Switching to data residency and retention: what do you need from us — specific policies or specific retention values?
[04:27] Laura Martinez: Our policy matrix: PII conversational transcripts — 1 year; security logs — 7 years; model artifacts metadata — 3 years. we need confirmation these classes are supported.
[04:36] Priya Nair: Should be doable — hosted can meet these with export/archival; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. we'll draft a mapping of Redwood retention config to your policy classes.
[04:46] Daniel Brooks: On compliance scanning — we need assurance of vulnerability scanning cadence and SCA for dependencies. is that in the SOC2 report or separate?
[04:55] Alex Chen: The SOC2 covers change management and patching cadence at a high level; we'll add our internal vuln scanning cadence and SCA results summary to the pack.
[05:03] Maya Patel: For the SIEM forwarding, do you preserve log ordering? sometimes events get re-ordered which makes incident reconstruction hard.
[05:11] Priya Nair: We keep timestamps and sequence numbers; reordering can happen on transit but we include sequence ids to reconstruct order. we'll include details.
[05:19] Laura Martinez: Can we get a sample of the exported file format (CSV/JSON) — that will help our SIEM team ingest.
[05:25] Priya Nair: Yes, sample export will be included.
[05:29] Daniel Brooks: Are there service accounts for automation? we need least privilege roles for rotating keys and pulling logs.
[05:36] Priya Nair: We support role-based access controls (RBAC) — admin, ops, auditor — and service principals that can be scoped down. we'll send role mapping.
[05:44] Omar Ruiz: A procurement note — please include SLAs and escalation matrix; we may need a dedicated support contact if we move to Dedicated.
[05:51] Alex Chen: We'll attach SLA doc and name of the enterprise success rep.
[05:55] Jordan Lee: On the POC tuning side, we also ran a few latency tests with batching enabled; saw 15-20% improvement but we need to confirm no logging gaps with batching.
[06:06] Priya Nair: Good point — batching aggregates tokens server-side; we still emit per-request audit entries, but in some high-throughput paths a single micro-batch may summarise per-call token counts. we'll produce a test artifact proving per-request visibility.
[06:19] Laura Martinez: Anything about data deletion? how do we handle deletion requests during the POC?
[06:24] Alex Chen: For hosted POC we can delete conversational transcripts on request; for Dedicated/Private you control deletion. Priya will outline the deletion API.
[06:31] Priya Nair: There's a delete-by-id and delete-by-user API, plus background garbage collection. note: transcripts backed into backups may have separate TTLs; we'll document recovery windows.
[06:41] Daniel Brooks: Can we perform a mock data subject request as part of the pilot to validate the workflow?
[06:46] Priya Nair: Yes, we can orchestrate a mock DSAR — we'll work with Maya to pick records.
[06:50] Maya Patel: I'll volunteer a dataset and coordinate with Priya.
[06:54] Alex Chen: Quick recap and owners. Alex to share SOC2 and pen test, Priya to re-run SSO config and sample logs, Maya to send SIEM details and retention matrix, Daniel to confirm network egress constraints, Omar to send legal questions.
[07:06] Laura Martinez: Timeline: can we have the SOC2 and sample logs by next Tuesday? that's the 6th.
[07:12] Alex Chen: Yes, we'll aim for that.
[07:14] Jordan Lee: I'll schedule a follow-up demo with the security team to walk through logs — propose Friday next week?
[07:20] Laura Martinez: Friday works, please send calendar invite.
[07:23] Alex Chen: Perfect — any other open risks?
[07:27] Daniel Brooks: Only the SSO ACS mismatch but that's small.
[07:30] Priya Nair: I'll send troubleshooting steps after the call.
[07:34] Alex Chen: Ok thanks all. we'll close the call.

End of transcript.

References/Shared artifacts mentioned:
- SOC2 Type II report (to be shared privately)
- Penetration test summary (redacted/public + full under NDA)
- POC audit log sample (CSV/JSON)
- SSO/SAML metadata + troubleshooting checklist
- Network manifest (outbound IPs/domains, ports)

Meeting Recap (auto):
- Redwood to provide compliance artifacts and technical docs to validate SOC2, KMS, RBAC, log forwarding, and retention mapping.
- Customer to provide SIEM endpoint and retention matrix; will validate SSO config and run mock DSAR.
- Next sync/demo scheduled for next Friday to review logs and SSO test.
